 - Vs -
Accused No. 1. Devaraju.H,
 S/o.Hanumanthappa,
 Aged about 32 years,
 2. Smt.VijayaLakshmi,
 W/o.Hanumanthappa,

 S/o.Late.Doddabajjaiah,

1

 Judgment
The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of Mahalakshmi Layout police
station against the accused No.1 to 3 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A r/w
Sec.
34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.

2 . In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the marriage of the accused No.1 was solemnized with C.W.1 on 04.05.2017 at Laggere, Manjushree Kalyan Mantapa,
Bengaluru as per Hindu rites and customs.

At the time of marriage the accused No.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence, in furtherance of their common intention received 139 grams of golden ornaments as dowry and after marriage of the C.W.1 while she has been residing with the accused No.1 along with her mother in law and father in law at the matrimonial house at Kempegowda Layout, Laggere, where the accused persons demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25 lakhs from her parental house and they extended physical and mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and assaulted her and therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused No.1 to 3 before the Mahalakshmi Layout Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.147/2020 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused No.1 to 3, for which C.C.20477/2020 charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, in persuance of summons the accused No.1 to 3 appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused No.1 to 3, therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 3 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 11 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

2 6.

Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused No.1 to 3 .
7.

In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of the accused No.1 was solemnized with C.W.1 on 04.05.2017 at Laggere, Manjushree Kalyan Mantapa, Bengaluru as per Hindu rites and customs and after marriage while C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house Laggere, Kempegowda Layout along with accused No.1 to 3, the accused with an intention to commit offence, in furtherance of their common object, C.C.20477/2020 unnecessarily picked up quarrel with C.W.1 for petty reasons and caused physical and mental cruelty to her by demanding C.W.1 to get additional dowry of Rs.25,00,000/- from her parents and thereby the accused No.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforementioned date, time and place, at the time of marriage on demand of accused No.1 to 3 the parents of CW.1 have provided 139 grams of gold ornaments in the form of dowry and thereby the accused have committed an offence punishable under section 3 of D.P. Act?
3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforementioned date, time and place, after marriage of CW.1 the accused No.1 to 3 have demanded cash of Rs.25,00,000/- as additional dowry and thereby the accused persons have committed the offence punishable under section 4 of D.P.Act?
4. What Order?
8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the 'Negative' Point No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.
The C.W.1 being complainant as well as Smt. Chaithra vs Devaraju H on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14840709/

3 victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 and 2 documents got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name C.C.20477/2020 Chaitra and she deposed in her evidence that accused No.1 is her husband and accused no.2 and 3 are the parents of accused No.1.
Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused No.1, the accused persons did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to Mahalakshmi Layout PS in the year 2020 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused No.1 to 3 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 3 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 3 beyond all reasonable doubt.
C.C.20477/2020 Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused No.1 to 3 , for which, I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.4:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 3 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 to 3 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 to 3 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused No.1 to 3 are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
